title: Representation Drift Lab
course: Cornell Tech CS 5787 Deep Learning; independent post-course extension
oneLine: An interactive, reproducible study of how adapting a vision–language model can change what it retains—built around evidence, uncertainty, and failure cases.
role: Ali Hasan: independent post-course extension, reproducibility system, interactive experience, and evidence audit. Original course report credits Sahil Mhatre, Ali Hasan, and Corey Chen.
primaryMetric: Nine local adaptation approaches evaluated across three independent seeds with 95% Student-t intervals (preliminary evidence).

thumbnail.alt: Representation Drift Lab thumbnail showing a new-task gain, a retained-task decline, and a preliminary three-seed evidence label.

initialEvidenceDeployment.note: The original immutable evidence-release deployment. The stable alias subsequently advanced for metadata-only and packaging-only follow-ups; neither changed the preliminary evidence bundle.

evidence.metric: Standard LoRA local adaptation and retention change
evidence.value: +6.9 percentage points on Food-101; -3.3 percentage points on CIFAR-10
evidence.sample: 3 independent seeds; 6 Food-101 classes with 24 train and 24 held-out evaluation images per seed; 30-image CIFAR-10 retained probe
evidence.scope: Local preliminary evidence; not a general model-ranking claim.

evidence.value: 9 interventions × 3 independent seeds with 95% Student-t intervals
evidence.sample: One CLIP backbone and bounded local subsets
evidence.scope: Preliminary local comparison; methods have different resource assumptions.
